unit.name: Honey, We Shrunk Ourselves × Los Angeles

situation.text: Hoje você conhece Marco, de Los Angeles. Tamanhos de roupa e provar.

pages.goal: Hoje você aprende a apontar coisas com this (perto) e that (longe), perguntando tamanhos numa loja de roupas.
canDo: Say: Can I try it on?

pages.hook: In US stores, clothes often come in letter sizes like S, M and L, and the numbers can change from brand to brand. Learn how to ask for the right size.
pages.polite: Say **“Excuse me, do you have this in a medium?”** A smile and **“Thank you!”** go a long way in a shop.

mythfact.s: Many US stores use letter sizes such as S, M and L for shirts.
mythfact.why: S, M, L and XL are very common on T-shirts and sweaters.

mythfact.s: A medium is always the same size in every store.
mythfact.why: Brands often cut clothes differently, so it is smart to try things on.

mythfact.s: In the USA you can never try clothes on in a shop.
mythfact.why: Most clothing stores have fitting rooms where you can try things on.

mythfact.s: “On sale” means the price is lower than usual.
mythfact.why: A sale is a time with lower prices.

compare.br: In Brazil many shops use numbers like 38 or 40 for clothes and also P, M and G for shirts.
compare.us: In the USA you often see S, M, L and numbers like 6 or 8 for dresses and pants, and the sizes change by brand.
compare.tip: Learn your size in English: small, medium, large. If you are not sure, ask: “Can I try it on?”

pages.title: Cultural spotlight
Reading quest — Too small, too big
text: In the 1997 family film **Honey, We Shrunk Ourselves**, the actor Rick Moranis plays an inventor. A machine makes people very tiny, and the adults must walk across a garden. For them, a button looks like a plate.
Now think about a normal day in a shop in Los Angeles. Wendy says to the clerk, “Hi, **I’m looking for** a T-shirt.” The clerk asks, “**What size are you?**” “I’m a medium,” she says.
The clerk brings a few shirts. “**Is this my size?**” Wendy asks. She holds the first one. It is too big. “**It’s too big**,” she says. The second shirt is too small. “**It’s too small**.”
“Can I **try it on**?” Wendy asks about a third one. The clerk smiles. “Sure. The fitting room is over there.” Wendy goes in. Then she comes out and looks in the mirror.
“**It fits well**!” she says. She asks, “Do you have it in blue?” “Yes, here you go,” says the clerk. The shirt is on sale, too.
Wendy pays and says, “Thank you!” Size is a small thing, but it changes your whole day.
